title: Model 2 track-history correction on Caribbean drifters
scope: Correction that hindcasts an object over its last 24 hours, measures the error, and carries a fading fraction of it forward. Needs a tracked object. Tested on undrogued surface drifters; settings chosen on one period and scored on the other.
summary: On 1,786 cases (2022-24) and 1,985 cases (2018-22), the correction cut the 48 h miss by 19.1% and 22.4% for the current-only recipe and by 21.8% and 27.4% for the wind-added recipe (intervals exclude zero), and the 120 h miss by 9% to 18%. Both directions chose the same setting: 24 h of history, 0.75 of the measured error, 4-day fade. When the history window was ended 12 h before issue to remove a possible interpolation leak, the 48 h gain fell to 11.6% to 14.8%, so 12 to 15% is a conservative floor.

limitations: The source report is an untracked working-tree file; it is identified by SHA-256 only and has no source commit.

Drifter positions are an interpolated six-hourly product, so the position at issue time may be partly built from later fixes; the lagged-window check removes most of this but cannot separate leak from information decay.
Drifters are undrogued surface drifters, not Sargassum, and the arms use analysis fields in place of forecasts.
Gains shrink with imprecise fixes: about 14 to 19% at 2 km noise and 8 to 11% at 5 km with retuned settings.
Borrowing the correction of nearby tracked objects for an untracked one is null (1 to 5% worse).
Tracked-object correction on Sargassum-like suites did not confirm; see the separate record.
